artifacts.summary: 11-phase migration of 17 of 19 extensions' source index-entries.json to the reconciled schema. Honors the research report's six corrections (147 description entries not 166; tags in 6 not 10 extensions; two orphan-risk skills entries needing replacement hooks; core and email additionally in scope; formal's 40 load_when.topics hoist; founder's 11-entry array-union merge) and adds two live-audit refinements: email's 8 and filetypes' 9 load_when.languages arrays are empty so they are deletions not renames, and the corpus is 461 entries not 470. Phases 2-10 are territory-disjoint per-extension and run in parallel.

memory_candidates.content: When planning a schema-conformance migration driven by a lint gate, re-run the live gate at plan time and treat its per-category output as the authoritative scope, never the task description's summary counts. A task description's enumerated WORK items are a hypothesis about the gate's true-positive set and routinely under-scope it: a live audit of an index-entries schema migration found the description's stated entry count inflated by ~13%, one named transform applying to only 6 of 10 listed targets, two additional extensions in scope that no WORK item named, and an entire violation category (a key nested one level too deep) omitted from the description while still required by the stated verification bar. A second, generalizable trap in any 'rename key X to key Y' migration: partition the target set by whether the value is EMPTY before renaming. Empty arrays rename into inert keys that satisfy no routing query, so they are deletions, not renames -- and any target already carrying BOTH the old and new key needs an array union, since a uniform rename silently overwrites the more specific pre-existing values. Both partitions are cheap to confirm with a jq probe and expensive to discover mid-implementation.
